title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 2 diabetes.

HPI
The patient is an 81-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that he has been managing his glucose levels with a combination of long-term insulin and an oral hypoglycemic agent. He states that he feels well and has not experienced any acute issues since his last visit. He denies any recent symptoms or concerns regarding his glucose levels.

Medication List
- Insulin glargine
- Metformin 500mg BID

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. Skin is intact with no signs of infection or breakdown. Pulse is 72 bpm, blood pressure is 128/82 mmHg, and oxygen saturation is 98% on room air.

Assessment
Type 2 diabetes without complications.

Plan
The patient will continue his current regimen of insulin and metformin. We will monitor his laboratory results at the next visit. He was instructed to contact the office if he experiences any new symptoms.

Electronically signed,
J. Lindqvist, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: No complication is documented: type 2 diabetes without complications.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Nothing in the note documents hyperglycemia or poor control.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
